checks: API exact serialized context, pre-I/O reservation, real per-request usage receipt and final proof settle through the lifecycle without legacy Run handling
API tool loop reserves each HTTP separately and continues Attempt heartbeats after the initial request is settled
HTTP 400 does not hide a compatibility retry; complete rejection retains unknown billing and unknown delivery rather than leaving a sending-only receipt
Truncated stream and missing terminal confirmation retain unknown execution and cannot produce a release proof
A later actual request becoming unknown preserves the first request’s confirmed usage and keeps the Attempt fence
Usage receipts bind the exact persisted request and fencing identity; changed usage, another generation and SQL mutation are rejected
SDK local protocol relay meters every hidden HTTP request, ignores cumulative SDK result usage and records a checkpoint only with exact native identity and input receipt
SDK resume preserves the trusted prior compaction boundary when no new compact event occurs; a new compact event replaces it and cold sessions never inherit it
SDK close notification without verified owned process-group exit cannot release resources or mint an anchor
Unexpected SDK session identity reaches the server reconciliation gate before any HTTP request or continuation
A proof snapshots request/process cardinality and cannot release the same claim after another request has appeared
Failure while persisting the pre-I/O backend receipt rolls back request start and quota changes before any transport call
Concurrent hidden SDK helper requests are serialized before request admission so a single resource claim never authorizes parallel actual HTTP calls
Endpoint prefixes are preserved, cached input contributes to total-token acceptance accounting, unknown cache tariffs remain unknown and other drivers stay closed
scope: isolated DB, injected HTTP responses, real loopback SDK relay; process-exit positives are explicitly injected protocol facts
